history.heading: Early peoples
paragraphs: San hunter-gatherers have lived in the Kalahari region for tens of thousands of years; the Tsodilo Hills contain thousands of rock paintings. Bantu-speaking farmers arrived later, and Tswana states emerged from around the 17th century.
In the 19th century the Tswana chiefdoms faced pressure from Boer settlers from the south and from Ndebele raids, and Christian missionaries such as David Livingstone were active.

history.heading: Bechuanaland Protectorate
paragraphs: In 1885, at the request of Tswana chiefs seeking protection from the Boers, Britain declared the Bechuanaland Protectorate. Three chiefs travelled to London in 1895 to prevent their land from being handed to Cecil Rhodes's British South Africa Company.
Britain invested little in the territory, which was poor and largely governed through traditional leaders.

history.heading: Independence
paragraphs: Botswana became independent on 30 September 1966 under Seretse Khama, a Tswana chief whose marriage to an Englishwoman, Ruth Williams, had caused a scandal in the colonial era. At independence it was one of the poorest countries in the world.

Diamonds were discovered shortly afterwards, and careful management of this wealth transformed the country. Botswana has held regular democratic elections ever since independence; in 2024 the Botswana Democratic Party lost power for the first time.

culture.heading: Society
paragraphs: Setswana is the national language and English the official language. The Tswana are the largest group, alongside Kalanga, San and others. Most people are Christian. The kgotla, a traditional community meeting place, remains important for discussion and dispute resolution.

Botswana is known for its wildlife, including the Okavango Delta, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and some of the largest elephant populations in Africa. Seswaa, pounded beef, is a national dish. The No. 1 Ladies' Detective Agency novels are set in Botswana.

politics.heading: Stable democracy
paragraphs: Botswana is a parliamentary republic in which the National Assembly elects the president, who is both head of state and government. It is often cited as one of Africa's most stable democracies with low corruption. In 2024 the Umbrella for Democratic Change won elections, and the transfer of power was peaceful.
The House of Chiefs (Ntlo ya Dikgosi) advises on matters of tradition.

economy.heading: Diamonds and beyond
paragraphs: Botswana is one of the world's largest diamond producers by value, mainly through Debswana, a joint venture between the government and De Beers. Diamond revenues financed infrastructure, education and health, making Botswana an upper-middle-income country.

Tourism and beef exports are also important. Weak global diamond demand in the 2020s highlighted the need to diversify. Challenges include inequality, unemployment and one of the world's highest HIV rates, though treatment programmes have been very successful. The currency is the pula.
